rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 2 (ki 0.9) scored 64.3, below iteration 1 (ki 0.3, score 71.2). Progress fell on every track (oval 0.263 to 0.226, s-bend 0.151 to 0.142, slalom 0.106 to 0.100), and max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.065 m, still past the 0.06 m limit. So the 'raise ki to cancel a steady bias' hypothesis is not supported. A stronger integral does not fix the drift and slightly slows the run. Steering oscillation stayed near 0.15, so the robot is not jittering. Every trial still leaves the line at about 0.063 m, with one line-loss event per run.

Changes. (1) controller.ki goes back to 0.3, the best-scoring value so far. (2) controller.kp goes from 3.0 to 4.0. The error that grows on bends needs a stiffer proportional correction, and max_error is the binding failure. (3) controller.kd goes from 0.15 to 0.2 to damp the stiffer response and keep steering_oscillation under about 0.2. Geometry and base_speed 1.3 are unchanged, so the race shows the effect of the steering gains alone.

Expected result. max_error falls below about 0.058 m, line_loss_events drop toward 0 on some seeds, and progress rises on the oval and s-bend. Steering oscillation should stay under about 0.2.

Risks and next steps. A higher kp can overshoot and raise steering_oscillation. If that happens, raise kd toward 0.25 before changing kp again. If max_error still sits near 0.06 with no oscillation, next try kp about 5 or move the sensors forward (y about 0.06) for earlier look-ahead. If progress reaches about 0.995 with no line loss, raise base_speed toward 1.8. Completion within 3 s is not expected at base_speed 1.3.

Measurements wanted: max_error, line_loss_events, progress, steering_oscillation, control_effort, rms_error, and completion_time.
